text: Dec 3, 2011 · Australian aboriginal artist Billy Yarrawanga travelled wide with his art to spread the wisdom of his land and culture. Who is Dalabon Aboriginal cultural experiences? Dalabon Aboriginal Cultural Experiences is a 100% Aboriginal-owned and operated tourism business located in Katherine, Northern Territory. Operated by multi-award-winning cultural guide Manuel Pamkal, the business provides authentic day tours, custom group itineraries, and art workshops. What language is Dalabon? Dalabon is also known as Dangbon (the Kune or Mayali name), Ngalkbun (the Jawoyn name), and Buwan (the Rembarrnga name). Dalabon belongs to the Gunwinyguan languages branch of the Arnhem languages; its nearest relatives are Kunwinjku, Kune, Mayali (varieties often grouped together as Bininj Kunwok), and Kunbarlang. Is Dalabon a Gunwinyguan language? Dalabon is a Gunwinyguan language of Arnhem Land, Australia. It is a severely endangered language, with perhaps as few as three fluent speakers remaining as of 2018. Dalabon is also known as Dangbon (the Kune or Mayali name), Ngalkbun (the Jawoyn name), and Buwan (the Rembarrnga name). Where do the Dalabon live today? The Dalabon today mainly live in an area east of Katherine, in Wugularr (formerly Beswick), Barunga (formerly Bamyili), Bulman and Weemol.
